claims.claim: DDA2 Legions of Thyatis (1990) advised characterising an NPC by picturing him as an animal while describing him.
claims.source: John Nephew, DDA2 Legions of Thyatis (TSR, 1990), quoted by David Hartlage, DMDavid, 2024
claims.page: DDA2 Legions of Thyatis (1990) — Characterizing NPCs

claims.claim: The Hidden Halls of Hazacor (2018) told new DMs to replace unimportant sequences with a short summary.
claims.source: Scott Fitzgerald Gray, The Hidden Halls of Hazacor (2018), quoted by David Hartlage, DMDavid, 2024
claims.quote: you can give the players a short summary instead
claims.page: The Hidden Halls of Hazacor (2018) — Summarize the boring parts

claims.claim: Hartlage notes that the 1999 introductory modules printed scripted text for the DM to read to new players.
claims.source: David Hartlage, DMDavid, 30 Jan 2024, on Eye of the Wyvern (1999)
claims.quote: scripted text for the DM to read to new players

claims.claim: Hartlage describes a fourth-edition design goal of letting a casual DM simply buy an adventure and read its boxed text.
claims.quote: buy an adventure, read the boxed text
claims.page: Skill challenges satisfied three design goals

claims.claim: McKenzie dates the first appearance of boxed read-aloud text in D&D to the 1980 module The Hidden Shrine of Tamoachan.
claims.source: Brian McKenzie, Analog Game Studies, 18 Dec 2023
claims.page: section on descriptive text and 'at rise' descriptions

claims.claim: McKenzie argues D&D read-aloud text is the genre analogue of the theatre's 'at rise' stage description.
claims.source: Brian McKenzie, Analog Game Studies, 18 Dec 2023

claims.claim: The Hidden Shrine of Tamoachan's own instruction is that its read-aloud text hints at what may be done and that the DM answer questions only vaguely.
claims.source: Harold Johnson and Jeff R. Leason, The Hidden Shrine of Tamoachan (1980), quoted by Brian McKenzie (2023)
claims.quote: the DM should only provide vague information if questioned

claims.claim: McKenzie's summary of the function of read-aloud text is that it offers clues and frames narrative boundaries.
claims.source: Brian McKenzie, Analog Game Studies, 18 Dec 2023
claims.quote: It offers clues and the frames narrative boundaries

claims.claim: McKenzie states that Jennifer Grouling Cover's is perhaps the only academic discussion of read-aloud text in tabletop adventures.
claims.source: Brian McKenzie, Analog Game Studies, 18 Dec 2023
claims.quote: one of the few—perhaps the only—academic discussions

claims.claim: Michael Shea likens read-aloud text to the script of a Broadway show.
claims.source: Michael Shea, quoted by Brian McKenzie, Analog Game Studies, 2023
claims.quote: our read-aloud text is part of our script

claims.claim: A Twitter poll by D&D lead rules designer Jeremy Crawford drew 2,248 replies, of which 59.5% wanted occasional boxed text, 34.4% wanted lots and 6% wanted none.
claims.source: Jeremy Crawford's poll, reported by Brian McKenzie, Analog Game Studies, 2023

claims.claim: Merwin calls boxed text as much a part of D&D's history and brand as saving throws, hit points and armor class.
claims.source: Shawn Merwin, 'Let's Design an Adventure: Boxed Text', D&D Beyond, 2019
claims.quote: as much a part of D&D's history and brand

claims.claim: Merwin says the act of writing boxed text forces designers to think harder about their encounters.
claims.source: Shawn Merwin, 'Let's Design an Adventure: Boxed Text', D&D Beyond, 2019
claims.quote: to think harder about their encounters

claims.claim: A scholarly case study lists read-aloud text, player handouts, DM instructions and NPC dialogue among the five textual elements that carry an adventure's ideas.
claims.source: Brian McKenzie, Bret Zawilski and James Beirne, International Journal of Role-Playing 17, 2026
claims.quote: read-aloud text, player handouts, instructions to the Dungeon Master

claims.claim: Huddleston notes that many early tabletop rulebooks contain little prose or narrative, being given over to rules.
claims.source: Stefan Huddleston, Analog Game Studies, 18 Dec 2022
claims.quote: many early examples lack prose and narrative in favor of rules
